items.title: Democrats Clinch 258 House Seats, an Election-Year Record This Century
items.summary: After sweeping midterm wins, Democrats have secured the largest House majority in a national election for either party in three decades.

items.title: Democrat Chuck Hubbard Defeats 11-Term Republican Virginia Foxx in North Carolina
items.summary: Chuck Hubbard, a retired journalist, defeated Representative Virginia Foxx in a conservative district.

items.title: Republicans Debate Why They Lost the Midterms, and if Trump Is to Blame
items.summary: A divide is emerging in the party over what caused its wipeout midterm defeats, foreshadowing a battle over how to move forward before 2028.

items.title: Is Annie Andrews Too Real for the Senate? South Carolinians Are About to Find Out.
items.summary: The pediatrician, who once compared JD Vance to the herpes virus, notched one of the most shocking upsets of the midterm elections by defeating Senator Darline Graham.

items.title: COP31 Talks Collapse in Turkey in a Clash Over Fossil Fuels
items.summary: European and vulnerable nations rejected a proposed agreement after Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas.

items.title: How Melania Trump Found a Diplomatic Opening in the War in Ukraine
items.summary: The first lady, who has little experience in international affairs, developed back channels to key figures on both sides of the conflict through her longtime agent.

items.title: Fact-Checking Stephen Miller, the New White House Chief of Staff
items.summary: Mr. Miller has promoted some of the second Trump administration’s most egregious falsehoods about immigration policy, the economy and political opposition.

items.title: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
items.summary: China’s espionage agency has been running a secret campaign to help the country’s companies acquire advanced A.I. chips and to gather intelligence on the sector, officials say.

items.title: Scott Bessent Calls on Nvidia to Provide Answers on Chip Sales to China
items.summary: The treasury secretary said on CBS that it was too soon to say if Jensen Huang should return as the company’s chief executive.

items.title: Looking for the Formula to Stop an Apocalypse
items.summary: Mike Winer and his colleagues are trying to build a mathematical safeguard to keep A.I. under human control. They fear they are running out of time.

items.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
items.summary: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.

items.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
items.summary: South Africa is working to overcome a children's literacy crisis. In one Johannesburg township, a reading club is instilling a love of books in kids — and inspiring them to become authors.

items.title: Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels
items.summary: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels - the primary driver of global warming.

items.title: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
items.summary: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

items.title: NPR's Senior Podcast Challenge: Early entries we love
items.summary: People 65 and older have been submitting stories for a chance to win our grand prize — a visit to NPR watch your podcast air live on Weekend Edition. There's still time to enter!

items.title: He expected a small-business loan. He got a 7-year nightmare
items.summary: America's fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses is also one of the least regulated. One man has waged a long, lonely fight to recoup its punishing cost.

items.title: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
items.summary: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.

items.title: Google employees protest AI in schools policy
items.summary: More than 550 Google employees signed a petition to allow schools access to Search without AI. Parents and educators protested outside Google offices in 6 cities last week for the same ask.

items.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
items.summary: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

items.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
items.summary: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.

items.title: U.S. Army tells court it will go ahead with detonation in Iowa by Tuesday
items.summary: The Trump administration says an emergency provision allows it proceed despite a pending lawsuit by environmental groups.

items.title: Why this incoming congresswoman opposed Jeffries for speaker
items.summary: Rep.-elect Angela Gonzales-Torres on that decision and her goals in Congress.

items.title: Why Jackie Kennedy wore the gore-spattered suit all day (and why we won’t see it again)
items.summary: The raspberry pink jacket and skirt, stained with President John F. Kennedy's blood, may not be shown to the public until at least 2103.

items.title: He wrote personal notes on hundreds of Christmas cards every year
items.summary: A teacher who loved folk dancing. A father’s words of wisdom. Intimate obituaries, in 150 words or less.

items.title: The remarkable recovery of a National Guardsman shot near the White House
items.summary: A year after Staff Sgt. Andrew Wolfe was shot in the head, his mind and body are healing. But his life was turned upside down.

items.title: Trump keeps losing in court. Here’s how he gets what he wants anyway.
items.summary: Judges have been unable to slow or stop some of the administration’s highest-profile projects.

items.title: When Captain Kirk and Lieutenant Uhura kissed, and America was pretty okay with it
items.summary: On Nov. 22, 1968, William Shatner and Nichelle Nichols shared U.S. television’s first scripted kiss between Black and White characters. An expected backlash failed to materialize.

items.title: Was Trump’s news conference with Vance and Rubio an audition for 2028?
items.summary: Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are widely considered to be potential Republican presidential candidates.

items.title: Man convicted of starting deadly Palisades fire in California
items.summary: The Palisades fire destroyed more than 6,800 buildings across Los Angeles and Malibu, with officials estimating the damage bill at $25 billion.

items.title: Emergency medical services could be delivered by drones
items.summary: Pilot programs in the U.S. allow drones to transport medical items, which can include defibrillators, medicines or blood. Drone delivery of organs faces many hurdles.
